test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A medical store owner purchased medicines worth Rs. 18,000 from a company. He sold 2/5 part of the medicine at a 35% loss. On which gain, he should sell the rest of the medicines so that he has neither gain nor loss?
solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of the medicine = Rs. 18,000.

Sold 2/5 part of the medicine at a 35% loss.

**Formula Used:**

Let the required gain percentage be G%.

Loss = 35%

Part sold at loss = 2/5

Part remaining = 1 - 2/5 = 3/5

Total cost price = Total selling price for no loss no gain condition.

**Calculation:**

Cost price of 2/5 part = (2/5) × 18000 = Rs. 7200

Loss on this part = 35% of 7200 = (35/100) × 7200 = Rs. 2520

Selling price of this part = 7200 - 2520 = Rs. 4680

Cost price of remaining 3/5 part = (3/5) × 18000 = Rs. 10800

Let the selling price of the remaining part be Rs. x.

For no gain no loss, total cost price = total selling price

18000 = 4680 + x

x = 18000 - 4680

x = Rs. 13320

Gain on remaining part = Selling price - Cost price = 13320 - 10800 = Rs. 2520

Gain% = (Gain / Cost price of remaining part) × 100 = (2520 / 10800) × 100

Gain% = (2520 / 10800) × 100

Gain% = 23(1/3)%

**The required gain percentage is 23(1/3)%.**
